title: Taming implies compatibility on four-manifolds
main_claim: Every smooth almost complex structure J on a closed four-manifold that is tamed by a symplectic form is also compatible with some symplectic form (Donaldson's tamed-to-compatible question). The paper also describes the compatible cone as the classes in C=K^t∩(H_J^-)^⊥ that pair strictly positively with the closure of C. The cones agree when h_J^-=b_2^+-1, and a T^4 example shows the inclusion can be strict.
coverage:
I read every section (1–8) and checked each step of the main proof line by line.
(1) Closed lift B=dd*G+H: L=Rdd* has symbol |ξ|^2/2 on im R ⊂ Λ^+, its kernel is closed, and RB=LG+H=Id. T=P+Q is closed and Q is anti-invariant and self-dual.
(2) Quadratic mass growth: Du=(1-BR)dd^c u is closed and invariant. The Hessian trace bounds 2s^2/(s^2+t^2)^2 and 1/sqrt(s^2+t^2) hold. The order-zero ΨDO correction bounds C/(s+t) and C(1+|log|) follow from the dyadic shells, and the sqrt term absorbs the negative parts.
(3) Kernel decomposition of S_r^2 from the gamma-weighted heat kernel: the r^-4 leading term, the lower bound on d<r, and the r^-2 error.
(4) Angular identity <l,*τm> = |l-τm|^2/2 - |F-τF|^2/4: verified algebraically using *l=F-l.
(5) Mixing lemma: ΠU=S_r[A_r,Π]U, and ||S_r||_{L2→H^{2j-1}} ≤ r^{-(2j-1)} gives O(r).
(6) Energy identity: the sign bookkeeping gives ||S_rQ|| bounded, ang_r=O(r^4) and Q∈L^2. The cross-term vanishing follows from density of smooth forms plus the uniform bound.
(7) Density monotonicity: the φ_r-φ_s test gives b(s)-b(r)=½T(1_ann dd^c log t) ≥ -Cs. The J-J_0=O(t) error and the anti-invariant part of size O(1/t) are both controlled by σ(B_s) ≤ Cs^2.
(8) Planar tangent measures: the closed constant-polarization limit A(p)ν; rank 4 is excluded by θD^2 growth; complex rank one forces λ_p to be a Dirac mass; ν=(θ/π)L^2_L; so trans_r=o(r^2).
(9) Splitting: the first variation df_r e_i = -r^{-2}∫∂_i h_r dμ; the comparison error is O(r) after integration over λ; closure on d(h_r dz_j) moves the derivative to normal directions with mixed forms O(δ+r^2); Cauchy–Schwarz gives r^-3·O(r^2)·o(r). The Q cutoff error goes to zero via θ=0 for volume-a.e. point and dominated convergence. The b_n limit is taken in the correct order.
(10) Final pairing: T'=T-P_E is closed; the negative error vanishes because the centres outside E have zero density; this forces Q=0, and P(ω)>0 gives the contradiction.
Cones section: I checked the H^2 = V ⊕ H_J^- decomposition, prescribed-class separation (the functional is constant on the affine space and c≤0), the taming criterion via closed positive currents, the residual lemma's o(s^2) cross-mass bound via a maximal s-separated cover, the y∈closure(C) argument, and the corollary via signature (1,b^-). I verified the T^4 example by hand: F has norm squared 2; η is closed, invariant, and its non-sine part is exact; H_J^-=0; U±V_0 tame J; and (U+V_0)·(U-V_0)=0.
I found no unjustified step, sign error or misapplied cited result. The one external input I did not re-derive is the cited heat-kernel parametrix and Gaussian bounds (Ludewig).
